core_obligations: Choose comparison quasi-isomorphisms a: K to K_1 and b: M to M_1, verify that they induce a homotopy equivalence on stalks for the total tensor products, hence a quasi-isomorphism, and conclude that K and M may be replaced by K_1 and M_1 (proof lines 7581-7606).
In the flasque case, write down the comparison diagram between the tensor product of global sections and the tensor product of total Cech complexes (proof lines 7608-7639).

Show that the horizontal arrows of that diagram are isomorphisms in D(A) by combining flasque acyclicity, the Leray acyclicity lemma and the Cech complex computation of derived global sections (proof lines 7640-7651).
Deduce the commutativity of the diagram of the lemma from the compatibility of the naive cup product with the derived one for the morphism to a point (proof lines 7652-7656).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the case where the Godement resolutions apply (proof lines 7581-7606).
Build the comparison diagram in the flasque case (proof lines 7608-7639).
Verify the horizontal arrows are isomorphisms in D(A) (proof lines 7640-7651).
Transfer commutativity from the known compatibility of the naive and derived cup products (proof lines 7652-7656).
difficulty_reason: For a ringed space (X, O_X), bounded below complexes K and M of O_X-modules and an open covering, the lemma asserts that a specific three-by-three diagram comparing the total Cech complexes, the tensor product, and the derived global sections commutes in D(A) (statement lines 7543-7578). The proof first replaces K and M by complexes K_1, M_1 for which the comparison maps of the Godement resolution type are available: since those maps are homotopy equivalences on stalks, the induced map on the total tensor products is a homotopy equivalence on stalks and hence a quasi-isomorphism, so the two targets agree in D(A) (proof lines 7581-7606). It then builds the comparison diagram in the flasque case (proof lines 7608-7639), shows the horizontal arrows are isomorphisms in D(A) by combining flasque acyclicity, the Leray acyclicity lemma and the Cech-to-derived comparison (proof lines 7640-7651), and finally reads off commutativity from the already established compatibility of the naive and derived cup products applied to the morphism to a point (proof lines 7652-7656). The claim is H2: two explicit reduction steps plus a diagram chase whose individual inputs are all standard, with no new construction.
